research_question: Which candidate rice lines have the highest model-predicted 100-grain weight (GRWT100) among the 904 candidates?
control_variables: Single fixed trained Ridge model (alpha=1000, 2000 pruned SNPs)
execution_evidence: run_model(capability=rank_candidates) invoked with all 904 candidate ids from /data/mzb/paper2agent/m2a_data/research/inputs/rice_candidates.json; returned 904 ranked records (verified 0 missing, 0 extra).
uncertainty: Held-out Spearman ~0.45; individual rank-1 prediction is not a guarantee. Prediction magnitude is biased low relative to measured values.
conclusion: The rice_gs Ridge model scored all 904 candidate lines (predicted GRWT100 range 1.499-3.662). Predictions are E1 only; no measured value is claimed here.
limitations: predictions are compressed/magnitude-biased and must be validated by phenotyping. E1 predictions are not measurements.

research_question: Which candidate line has the highest real measured 100-grain weight (GRWT100) among the candidates?
model: rice_gs (E1 predictions) + evidence oracle (E3 measured GRWT100)
control_variables: measured via the single evidence oracle
all 20 queries drawn from the model top-20 for comparability.
uncertainty: Residual risk the global maximum is an unmeasured line: measured values among top-20 spanned 2.8-5.0 g, and a rank-14 predicted line (IRIS_313.12349, pred 3.302) measured 4.7, showing appreciable prediction-error scatter. Best estimate of the maximum is IRIS_313.12254 (5.0 g); margin over the next measured line is 0.3 g.
conclusion: Among 20 measured lines (the top-20 model-ranked), the highest measured GRWT100 was IRIS_313.12254 = 5.0 g, which was also the model's rank-1 prediction. Spearman(predicted, measured)=0.473 (p=0.035), confirming enrichment: the model ranking is informative for high grain weight. E1 rank-1 candidate is supported by E3 measurement.
limitations: Only 20 of 904 lines measured (top-20 by prediction, no low-rank controls), so the true pool maximum could lie in the unmeasured set. Single environment
no GxE. No replicate measurements, so measurement error is not characterized.
